summary: Checked all 11 estimate records against the complete 203-line markdown conversion and all six PDF pages, including references; inspected Figure 1 in memory and recovered Tables II and III with pymupdf.find_tables. There is no appendix or embedded supplement. All recorded numerical statistics and study counts match the PDF: AUT average-distance NoAI coefficient -0.002 (SE 0.044), HighRandomness -0.008 (0.037); AUT maximum-distance NoAI -0.003 (0.054), HighRandomness -0.012 (0.045); RAT NoAI -0.044 (0.055), HighRandomness -0.074 (0.049); pooled RAT AI and no-AI accuracy 55% and 45%, p < .05. The study retains 775 people, with Table I counts 76, 69, 68, 84, 78, 83, 106, 106, 105 in the named column order. Recruitment of 960 does not establish the randomized count, and no analysis-specific counts are printed for the estimates; the corresponding nulls are justified. The two mechanical quote-not-found warnings are false positives caused by intervening table columns in linear PDF text. Table II, PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1773), contains NoAI -0.003 (0.054) and HighRandomness -0.012 (0.045) in Max Semantic Distance. Neither is a numerical or source-location error. The 20 problem entries comprise 10 scope errors (six numerical condition regressions and four DAT placeholders from models adjusted for post-treatment AI use and task duration), seven se_basis vocabulary conflicts for an unreported independence basis, and three unsupported RAT automated_score classifications. The latter two categories are coding gaps with no confirmed replacement, not invitations to guess. The full-sample pooled RAT comparison is already present and is not described as restricted to actual AI users; its numerical values are confirmed. The later RAT 64%, 72%, and 57% results and AUT 0.51 versus 0.31 result are actual-user subgroups and correctly excluded. No additional identifiable eligible full-sample outcome or contrast is missing under rules 4 to 6. The self-report measures, baseline fluency, pilot, AI-uptake outcomes, and self-selected-use associations are correctly omitted. Question, construct, direction, AI availability, immediate timing, between-person comparison coding, and named arms are otherwise consistent with the paper. Within-person variety is flexibility, not across-person diversity. Three rounds within one assigned condition do not make a crossover design. No after_ai or across_people outcome is reported. The observation unit, aggregation across rounds, and uncertainty basis remain insufficiently specified; no participant-level precision is inferred.
